originality.rationale: PASS, qualified: Ball–Gárgyán 2026 introduce exactly this balanced discrete score, prove the unquantified convolution information inequality and characterize binomial extremizers of an associated Cramér–Rao inequality. The nonnegative adjacent-pair quantitative remainder, explicit TV closeness from score increments, and optimal square-root deficit exponent were not identified in the materially read sections of their primary paper. Nishiyama and Gibilisco–Isola use different discrete information frameworks. The adjacent-edge estimate is elementary once the prior variance identity is known, but the connected quantitative inverse theorem is a natural new consequence; an implicit earlier stability estimate remains possible.
residual_risks: A stronger unpublished or unindexed discrete-score stability theorem could imply this adjacent-fiber bound.
The coefficient c degenerates with minimum atom mass; neither dimension-free nor globally sharp constants are established.

value.rationale: PASS: Stability of equality in an information inequality is a standard mathematically motivated gap, not just a rephrased nonnegative deficit. The result identifies the exact extremizers, quantitatively forces both score sequences toward affine increments, bounds total variation to balanced binomial laws, and gives a sharp local square-root exponent while transparently retaining mass-sensitive constants.

limitations: All coordinates positive, contiguous finite supports and alternating-balance; a,b>0.
TV bound is local under tau_f<=2/m and min-mass-dependent.
No claim that a generic discrete Fisher notion shares this normalization.
